t.7.41.1: Then the mighty-armed Rāma, having dismissed the gold-adorned Puṣpaka, entered the Aśoka grove.
t.7.41.2: It was adorned on every side with sandalwood, agaru and mango trees, with tall kāleyaka trees, and with groves of devadāru as well.
t.7.41.3: It was thickly covered with priyaṅgu and kadamba trees, with kurabakas as well, and with jambū, pāṭalī and kovidāra trees.
t.7.41.4: At all times it was adorned with lovely blossoms and with charming fruit-bearing growth, rich in beautiful shoots and flowers and thronged with intoxicated bees.
t.7.41.5: It was adorned with cuckoos, bhṛṅgarāja birds and hundreds of bright birds of many colours, which sat upon the mango trees like ornaments upon their crests.
t.7.41.6: There the trees shone forth, some resembling refined gold, some like tongues of flame, and others like dark collyrium.
t.7.41.7: There were long ponds of various shapes, filled with excellent water, with steps of precious gems and pavements of crystal between them.
t.7.41.8: The pools there were thick with blooming lotuses and water lilies and graced by cakravāka birds, and they were adorned with walls of many shapes and with slabs of stone.
t.7.41.9: Here and there in the parts of the grove, they were richly endowed with grassy lawns resembling vaiḍūrya gems and adorned with flowering trees.
t.7.41.10: Just as Indra's Nandana and Brahmā's Caitraratha are, of such a form was that grove laid out for Rāma.
t.7.41.11: Having entered the flourishing Aśoka grove, furnished with many seats and pavilions and enclosed by bowers of creepers, the delight of the Raghus…
t.7.41.12: Rāma then sat down upon a seat of beautiful form, adorned with clusters of flowers and covered with a spread of fine woollen cloth.
t.7.41.13: Taking Sītā in his arms, Kākutstha made her drink the finest madhumaireya wine, just as Indra makes Śacī drink amṛta.
t.7.41.14: For Rāma's meal, the servants swiftly brought various kinds of meat and diverse fruits.
t.7.41.15: Women skilled in dance and song, young and beautiful, who had fallen under the sway of drink, danced before the king.
t.7.41.16: Thus, day after day, Rāma, filled with joy, delighted Vaidehī, Sītā of the most lovely face, like a god.
t.7.41.17: And while the great-souled Rāghava, lord of men, was thus taking his delight, the auspicious days of the cool season passed by.
t.7.41.18: Having righteously discharged the affairs of the citizens in the forenoon, the knower of dharma spent the remaining half of the day within the inner apartments.
t.7.41.19: And Sītā, having performed the morning rites to the gods, stood with joined palms before all her mothers-in-law, honouring each of them alike.
t.7.41.20: Then she, adorned with many and varied ornaments, approached Rāma, just as Śacī approaches the thousand-eyed Indra seated in heaven.
t.7.41.21: But Rāghava, seeing his wife endowed with an auspicious condition, attained incomparable joy and said, "Excellent, excellent!"
t.7.41.22: O Vaidehī, this gain of offspring has come to me. What is it that you desire? Tell me that; what wish of yours shall be fulfilled?
t.7.41.23: Then Vaidehī, laughing, spoke these words to Rāma: "O Rāghava, I wish to see the holy penance-groves."
t.7.41.24: O hero, I long to see the hermitages on the bank of the Gaṅgā and to dwell at the feet of the sages of holy deeds who live on fruits and roots.
t.7.41.25: This is my highest desire, O Kākutstha: that I may dwell, even for a single night, among those rich in merit who live on roots and fruits.
t.7.41.26: And Rāma, of unwearied deeds, promised, saying, "So be it. Be at ease, Vaidehī; tomorrow you shall go, without doubt."
t.7.41.27: Having spoken thus to Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, Rāma, the descendant of Kakutstha, surrounded by his friends, went out into the middle chamber of the palace.
